name: fastcodon
summary: FastAPI rebuilt natively in Codon so that an ASGI-class web framework compiles to machine code, developed bottom-up against a published dependency graph with each layer marked verified as it lands. Sixty-four .codon files carry the stack from non-blocking sockets and a poll-based selector up through pure-Codon SHA-1, SHA-256, HMAC and base64, an HTTP parser, cancel scopes and task groups, chunked streaming and a WebSocket transport. The 57 from-C-import declarations sit in five files and are the platform boundary, covering both Winsock and BSD sockets.
why_codon: README states the framework is rebuilt natively in Codon so that it compiles to machine code and runs at native speed.
note: Writes its own crypto and socket layers in Codon rather than binding a C library, so it exercises the language more broadly than its single recorded feature suggests.

name: TurboX (sir-george2500)
summary: A Python backend framework built on the Codon compiler, layered over a server core called Nucleus that is itself written in Codon with C FFI. Nine .codon files hold the application layer and the server core; the six from-C-import sites are spread one per file rather than concentrated in a binding module.
why_codon: README states TurboX leverages Codon to compile Python code to machine code, delivering performance comparable to Rust and C++ without traditional interpreter overhead.
note: Shares a name with cruso003/TurboX and nothing else: the two have zero .codon paths in common and different layouts. Not a fork.

name: TurboX (cruso003)
summary: An alpha web framework built on the Codon compiler with first-class MCP support, pinning Codon 0.16 or later. Sixteen .codon files hold examples and feature tests rather than a large framework body, and the ten from-C-import sites are confined to two files. By the same author as Conduit, which is larger, later and carries the same MCP framing.
why_codon: README states it compiles Python-like code to native machine code via Codon, claiming performance comparable to Go and Rust and 10-100x faster than CPython.
note: README carries an MIT license badge linking to LICENSE, but the repo contains no LICENSE file. Conduit, by the same author, has the same discrepancy.
